display.title: Episode 476: Life in the Hands of the Tongue, Chapter 1 (Sefiras HaOmer)
display.summary_short: Counting the last days of exile, a young guest sings Ani Maamin, and a story about guarding our speech begins: a hunter brings a sick king lion's milk and dreams that his body parts are quarreling.
display.summary_long: Broadcast during Sefirah, 5751. Uncle Yossi teaches that as we count the Omer we are also counting the last days of exile, and that the Rambam lists belief in Moshiach's coming among the thirteen principles of faith. A young member of Tzivos Hashem sings Ani Maamin and talks about what he enjoys in the club, followed by how to join. Before story time, Uncle Yossi introduces the Chofetz Chaim's teachings on shemiras halashon: words are like an arrow, which cannot be called back once released, which is why Hashem placed the tongue behind teeth and lips. A girl recites the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. The story begins: a kind king falls gravely ill and can be cured only by lion's milk. A clever hunter wins a lion's trust with ten goats and fills a bucket, but on the way back he dreams that his feet, hands, brain, eyes and ears each claim the reward, and they all laugh at the tongue, who vows to prove he is king of the body. To be continued. The show ends with a listener's letter from New Jersey.
display.lesson: Guard your tongue: like an arrow, a word cannot be taken back once it is spoken.
